items.followUp: Why are gases more compressible than liquids?

rubric.why: Identifies the large separation between gas particles.
rubric.description: Gas particles are much farther apart than liquid particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that gas particles are far apart or have large spaces between them.

rubric.why: Connects particle spacing with the lower density of gases.
rubric.description: Their mass per unit volume is therefore lower than that of liquids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the particle spacing to lower density.

modelAnswer: Gas particles are much farther apart than particles in liquids.
Therefore, gases have less mass per unit volume and lower density.

items.followUp: Write the boiling points of water and acetone.

rubric.why: Gives the boiling point of di-ethyl ether.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct boiling point of di-ethyl ether.

rubric.why: Gives the boiling point of ethyl alcohol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct boiling point of ethyl alcohol.

modelAnswer: The boiling point of di-ethyl ether is about 34.6 °C.
The boiling point of ethyl alcohol is about 78.4 °C.

items.followUp: State two differences between a solution and a colloid.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the uniform nature of a solution from a suspension.
rubric.description: A solution is homogeneous, whereas a suspension is heterogeneous.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct contrast in composition.

rubric.why: Identifies a characteristic difference in particle behaviour.
rubric.description: Particles in a solution do not settle on standing, whereas suspension particles settle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct contrast in settling behaviour.

modelAnswer: A solution is homogeneous, whereas a suspension is heterogeneous.
The particles of a solution do not settle on standing, but the particles of a suspension settle.

items.followUp: Is dissolving ammonium chloride in water exothermic or endothermic? Explain its effect on the solution temperature.

rubric.why: Identifies the heat change during dissolution.
rubric.description: Dissolving KNO₃ in water is an endothermic process and absorbs heat.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that heat is absorbed.

rubric.why: Explains why the test tube feels cold.
rubric.description: The process takes heat from the water and surroundings, lowering their temperature and cooling the test tube.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking heat absorption to cooling.

modelAnswer: Dissolving KNO₃ in water is an endothermic process, so it absorbs heat.
The heat is taken from the water and surroundings, causing the test tube to become cold.

items.followUp: Define oxidation state and state the oxidation states of sodium and chlorine in NaCl.

rubric.why: Gives the meaning of oxidation state.
rubric.description: Oxidation state is the apparent charge assigned to an atom in a compound or ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example with correctly assigned oxidation states.
rubric.description: In NaCl, sodium has oxidation state +1 and chlorine has oxidation state −1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example and oxidation states.

modelAnswer: Oxidation state is the apparent charge assigned to an atom in a compound or ion.
For example, in NaCl, the oxidation state of Na is +1 and that of Cl is −1.

items.followUp: What is meant by the electropositive nature of an element?

rubric.why: Identifies the tendency that defines metallic character.
rubric.description: Metallic character is the tendency of an atom to lose electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an atom tends to lose electrons.

rubric.why: States the result of losing electrons.
rubric.description: By losing electrons, the atom forms positive ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that positive ions are formed.

modelAnswer: Metallic character is the tendency of an atom to lose electrons.
On losing electrons, it forms positive ions.

items.followUp: Give two physical properties that distinguish metals from non-metals.

rubric.why: Gives a valid contrast in physical form or mechanical behaviour.
rubric.description: Metals are generally malleable and ductile, while solid non-metals are generally brittle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct physical-property contrast.

rubric.why: Gives a valid contrast in conductivity.
rubric.description: Metals are generally good conductors of heat and electricity, whereas non-metals are generally poor conductors.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct conductivity contrast.

modelAnswer: Metals are generally malleable and ductile, whereas solid non-metals are generally brittle.
Metals are generally good conductors of heat and electricity, while non-metals are generally poor conductors.

items.followUp: Write a balanced equation for the reaction of fluorine with sodium.

rubric.why: Identifies the products formed when fluorine reacts with water.
rubric.description: Fluorine reacts with water to form hydrogen fluoride and oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both products or giving the correct balanced equation.
Award 1 mark for the correctly balanced equation.

modelAnswer: Fluorine reacts with water to form hydrogen fluoride and oxygen.
